name: Water
blurb: Clean enough to drink. Every liter is a piece of tomorrow.
foundLog: You shake a bottle and hear a slosh. Clean water.

name: Ration pack
blurb: Crash rations. Dry, salty, and more useful than pride.
foundLog: A ration pack, foil still intact, warm from the sun.

name: Cloth
blurb: Seat fabric and a shirt you are not wearing. Shelter wants it.
foundLog: You cut free a length of cabin cloth.

name: Debris
blurb: Struts, panel, and a tray. Enough to roof a scrape in the ground.
foundLog: You drag a usable piece of debris out of the gravel.

name: Stone
blurb: Rocks the size of a fist. A fire pit is a ring of these.
foundLog: You stack stones that will hold a fire.

name: Fuel bundle
blurb: Cushion foam, a tire strip, dry creosote sticks. One bundle feeds a signal fire for one night.
foundLog: You salvage a bundle of things that will burn.

name: Plastic sheet
blurb: Clear plastic from a window shade. A still needs a sheet that can sweat.
foundLog: A sheet of plastic, cracked at one corner and otherwise perfect.

name: Container
blurb: A cup, a bottle, a dented tin. Something to catch water under plastic.
foundLog: You pocket a container that will hold a cup of water.

name: Tubing
blurb: Oxygen line, still flexible. A still drinks through this without breaking the seal.
foundLog: You coil a length of tubing.

name: First aid kit
blurb: Gauze, a wrap, antiseptic that stings. It stops a bite from becoming the whole day.
foundLog: A first aid kit, latch gritty, contents still there.

name: Torn field manual
blurb: One charred page. A pit, a sheet of plastic, a cup, a tube.
foundLog: A charred page. Someone drew a still: plastic, a cup, a tube.

name: Barrel cactus
blurb: A ribbed green cactus. It looks like water.
foundLog: A barrel cactus, ribs swollen, as if it were saving something for you.

name: Prickly pear
blurb: Flat green pads with fine spines that want your fingers.
foundLog: Prickly pear pads, bright and armed.

name: Desert mistletoe berries
blurb: Translucent berries on a parasite shrub. They look like fruit.
foundLog: A cluster of pale berries on a shrub latched to a palo verde.

name: Creosote sprigs
blurb: Small resinous leaves. After rain they smell like the sky. This is not rain.
foundLog: Creosote sprigs, sticky and sharp-smelling.

name: Mesquite pods
blurb: Dry tan pods. Something sweet is packed in the fiber.
foundLog: You strip a handful of dry mesquite pods.

name: Seep water
blurb: A film of water in a low spot. It did not get there cleanly.
foundLog: Water darkens the sand in a low spot. You fill a container with the seep.

name: Factory knife
blurb: A folding knife with a real steel blade. Better than anything you can lash together, and it does not come apart on a miss.
foundLog: Half buried by a seat frame: a folding knife, blade still sound.

name: Club
blurb: A handle with a weight lashed to the end. Ugly reach, honest weight.
foundLog: A club.

name: Spear
blurb: A long shaft with an edge lashed to the tip. Reach is the whole point.
foundLog: A crude spear.

name: Torch
blurb: A handle with a flammable head. Each burn is one job's worth of light in the dark.
foundLog: A torch, unlit.

name: Rattlesnake meat
blurb: Pale, ropy meat. Real calories. It will not keep long in this heat.
foundLog: Rattlesnake meat.

name: Scorpion
blurb: A dead scorpion, stinger off. A mouthful, if that.
foundLog: A dead scorpion.

name: Crafted knife
blurb: An edge bound into a handle. It cuts. It is not a factory knife, and a miss can take it apart.
foundLog: A crafted knife.

name: Creosote stick
blurb: A short, straight creosote stem. A handle for a knife, a club, or a torch.
foundLog: You snap off a straight creosote stem. Handle length.

name: Mesquite branch
blurb: A long, straight mesquite branch with the thorns knocked off. Long enough for a spear.
foundLog: You work a straight mesquite branch loose and knock off the thorns.

name: Ironwood branch
blurb: Desert ironwood, dense as bone. The best long handle out here.
foundLog: A dead ironwood limb, heavy as a pipe. It will make a shaft that does not bend.

name: Seat strut
blurb: A short aluminum strut from a seat frame. A stiff handle.
foundLog: You unbolt a short strut from a broken seat frame.

name: Aluminum tube
blurb: A long, light aluminum tube from the cabin frame. Long enough for a spear.
foundLog: A long aluminum tube, bent at one end and straight enough.

name: Panel strip
blurb: A strip of cabin plastic. It will do as a grip. It will not do near a flame.
foundLog: You crack a strip of plastic off a cabin panel.

name: Plastic pipe
blurb: A length of plastic duct pipe. Long, but it bows.
foundLog: A length of plastic ducting, long and a little too bendy.

name: Glass shard
blurb: A curved shard from a window. Wickedly sharp, and brittle.
foundLog: You wrap a glass shard from a broken window in your sleeve.

name: Sheet-metal shard
blurb: A torn piece of fuselage skin. Grind it on a rock and it holds an edge.
foundLog: A torn tongue of fuselage skin. Grind it on a rock and it will cut.

name: Chert nodule
blurb: A glassy stone that breaks into flakes sharper than steel, if you know how to strike it.
foundLog: A waxy chert nodule. Struck right, it flakes like glass.

name: Metal fitting
blurb: A heavy seat-rail fitting and its bolt. Weight for the end of a club.
foundLog: You twist a heavy fitting off a seat rail.

name: Paracord
blurb: A hank of nylon cord. It binds anything you can tie.
foundLog: A hank of paracord, still coiled.

name: Wire
blurb: A length of wiring stripped from the wreck. Twists tight and does not burn.
foundLog: You strip a length of wire out of a torn panel.

name: Duct tape
blurb: Half a roll. Fixes most things. Melts near a flame.
foundLog: Half a roll of duct tape, sticky with dust.

name: Yucca leaves
blurb: Stiff, fibrous leaves. Pounded and twisted, they make cord.
foundLog: You cut a handful of yucca leaves. The fibers inside are long and strong.

name: Snake sinew
blurb: Sinew from a rattlesnake's back. The best binding you will find out here.
foundLog: You strip the sinew from the snake's back and set it to dry.
